title: Democrats Sweep: Will Farmers Still Get $8B in Aid?? + MONSTER Corn/Soybean Crop Estimates

bullets: Dec corn −2¼ at 440¼; overnight low 438½, a fresh low for the move
Jan beans −11½ at ~12.02, also fresh lows
Dec CBOT wheat unchanged at 599¾; KC +2½ at 638¾; MGEX +¼ at 619¾
Dems projected to win both chambers (per AP): at least 245 House seats; Senate flips in IA, KS, NC, OH, SC, TX
Likely Dem targets: Trump’s tariff authority, limits on Iran war funding, investigations, healthcare
$8B farmer fuel relief is safe because it went through USDA/CCC, not Congress. The extra aid Trump floated if the GOP won is now off the table
Hosts blame affordability (gas and diesel) for the GOP loss
Corn yield 183.1 bpa (prior 182.1) vs USDA 181.2; production 16.2B bu vs USDA 16.03B, about 169M bu above USDA
MN corn 207 vs USDA 195; StoneX also well above USDA in ND, SD, KS, WI, OH
Soy yield 55.0 bpa (prior 54.1) vs USDA 53.1; production 4.73B bu vs USDA 4.56B, about +163M bu
Hosts’ view: the price action suggests the trade is already using StoneX-type yields, not USDA’s
Dec corn about −6 to ~443, lowest settle since early July. It has gone from the July lows to the Sept highs and back
Jan beans −3 to 12.14. Weak even though export sales and crush are strong, so crop size is seen as the driver
Dec SRW wheat tested the July lows near 590½. The trade is ignoring Russia/Ukraine peace talk and focusing on bigger US winter wheat plantings
Flash sales: 12M bu corn to Mexico, 5M corn to S. Korea, 5M beans to unknown (all current MY)
Corn export book is about 34% behind last year, while USDA projects only about −4% for the year

ADM raised full-year guidance for the 3rd straight quarter. Ag Services & Oilseeds Q3 op profit $778M (more than doubled); crush $311M vs $13M a year ago. Stock −7% Tue on a revenue miss but +22.8% YTD
USDA cash crush margins: ~$4.30/bu IN/OH, $4.22 IL, under $4 MN/IA
126 in Oct vs 123 in Sept; current conditions +16, future expectations −2
Strong balance sheet: 62% vs 76% in Jan
35% think tariffs help ag vs 58% a year ago; 51% now say they hurt
Right direction: 48%, vs ~72–75% a year ago
S&P +~1% after a sharp drop overnight on the results. Tech was briefly hit on the Texas Dem governor’s stance on data centers, then recovered
Rates: Treasuries slightly firmer, USD slightly lower. No Fed comments
Dec WTI −0.87 at 95.22
ACA premiums expected +13% in 2027 after +26% this year. Host argues CPI’s health insurance index understates real premium inflation
